findings.description: Both messages explain why the change exists rather than restating the diff, and both carry the two facts the constitution names by hand.
findings.evidence:
d2a02f6 body: "An abandoned interactive rebase left this source dir detached on 2026-06-26. Every run after that committed onto the detached HEAD and reported success, so 26 commits piled up somewhere nothing could push them... It ran that way for six weeks" and "The guard deliberately runs before the clean-tree early exit rather than after it. A detached HEAD with nothing to commit is still a machine that can't pull". Both of the constitution's named facts (26 commits stranded for six weeks; clean-tree refusal as a deliberate choice) are present. It also records the precedence rationale and why recovery stays manual. No function list, no diff narration.
faba26f body: "Most of the file is the work of reaching the guard honestly... PATH is replaced rather than extended, apps.bats:73's form and not doctor.bats:62's" and "an empty one passes `test -f` and fails `git rev-parse --verify -q`, and the case would then be grading the guard on how the fixture happened to be built". Every mechanical detail it names is attached to the reason it was chosen.

findings.description: Each commit stands alone and is green at its own checkout, verified in detached worktrees so this checkout was never detached.
findings.evidence:
$ git worktree add --detach <scratch>/wt-d2a02f6 d2a02f6 ; bats <scratch>/wt-d2a02f6/tests/
EXIT=0 | plan 1..120 | ok 120 | not ok 0 | skip 0
$ git worktree add --detach <scratch>/wt-faba26f faba26f ; bats <scratch>/wt-faba26f/tests/
EXIT=0 | plan 1..125 | ok 125 | not ok 0 | skip 0
(last 5: ok 121 attached-commits-normally .. ok 125 clean-tree refusal)
Order is guard-then-tests, which is the only order satisfying green-at-checkout per the constitution's worker note. After removal: `git worktree list` shows only the main checkout, `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` -> refs/heads/main (exit 0), `git status --porcelain` -> 0 lines, HEAD = faba26fed35566084408fdc98c7abff1f6e8b800, unchanged.

findings.description: Folding T-004's clean-tree case into the same commit as T-002's four cases serves a future reader rather than hiding a boundary; judged not a violation.
findings.evidence: tests/sync.bats:183-199 is the clean-tree case. It calls `fresh_repo` (defined :107), uses `$DETACHED_MSG`/`$REBASE_MSG`/`$MERGE_MSG` (setup, :31) and `write_stubs` (:55) -- 18 lines that cannot run without the 107 lines of harness introduced in the same commit. Split out, it would be one case appended to a file its own parent commit created, which is a fixup in history terms. Nothing is concealed: the case is named in the subject ("and on a clean tree") and gets its own body paragraph -- "The clean-tree case is the one that was easy to leave out, and it covers the half of the fix aimed at `chezmoi update` rather than at `git push`... Nothing else here would notice." The T-002/T-004 boundary exists because B-5 was written mid-Phase-2 (constitution Revision 8); that is guild process history, already recorded in the constitution and task files, and of no use to a reader of this repo's log. D-3's text requires a commit to stand alone and explain itself, not to map one-to-one onto a task.

Added lines from `git diff 298c8a6..HEAD -- dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++' | sed 's/^+//'`: 23 raw, 15 after dropping whole-line comments -- non-empty, so the run is not void.
grep -nE "$pattern" over those added lines: no output, exit=1. Zero matches with a confirmed-live instrument. The guard's three conditions all use `[ ... ]` in `if`/`elif` position, never a bare `[[` or `((`.

findings.description: Re-run in committed form: every added line in the script belongs to refusing an unpushable source dir; no new phase, no change to an existing phase, no edit to the push-failure classifier.
findings.evidence: The whole committed change is one hunk, `@@ -129,0 +130,23 @@ cd "$SRC"`, so it lands between `cd "$SRC"` at :128 and the clean-tree exit at :130-133 and touches nothing else in the file. The 23 lines are: 8 comment lines recording the incident, the before-the-clean-tree-exit placement rationale and the markers-before-HEAD precedence rationale; then `if [ -d "$SRC/.git/rebase-merge" ] || [ -d "$SRC/.git/rebase-apply" ]; then` / `elif [ -f "$SRC/.git/MERGE_HEAD" ]; then` / `elif ! git symbolic-ref -q HEAD >/dev/null; then`, each arm being exactly notify_fail + echo + `exit 1` (the detached arm adds `head_sha="$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"`, used in both its messages); then `fi` and a blank line. Nothing added executes on a successful run. The push-failure classifier at :169-182 receives no added line -- the single hunk is 39+ lines above it. No `command -v` gate and no new phase heading appears anywhere in the added set. Both of D-4's measured escape examples are absent.
